sections.heading: Sepolia Fork Recap
sections.summary: The Sepolia Glamsterdam fork went well with no issues reported; the team is ready to move on to Hoodi.
sections.body:
- The Sepolia Glamsterdam fork was confirmed to have gone smoothly, with no notable issues raised by any client team.
- Barnabas noted that [glamsterdam-devnet-12](https://dora.glamsterdam-devnet-12.ethpandaops.io) launched the day before and was being shut down that day; builder deposits with invalid deposits were tested and all clients handled them correctly.

sections.heading: Hoodi Testnet Fork Preparations
sections.summary: Hoodi is scheduled for October 26; client releases are due imminently, with Teku, Lighthouse, and Grandine releases expected within days.
sections.body:
- Hoodi fork is scheduled for October 26 UTC.
- Only Lodestar and ethrex had published releases at the time of the call; the deadline for releases was the following day.
  - Teku confirmed release tomorrow.
  - Lighthouse planned early next week.
  - Grandine aimed for tomorrow or early next week.
- An EF blog post for Hoodi is ready pending a quorum of client releases; it will be published as soon as enough are available and updated later if needed.
- Barnabas urged testing builders at the fork transition on Hoodi, including making builder deposits and top-ups before the fork so builders can propose blocks in the first or second slot post-fork.
- Nico Flaig shared a builder onboarding landing page for Hoodi: [builder-hoodi.nflaig.dev](https://builder-hoodi.nflaig.dev/).

sections.heading: Builder Onboarding Deposit Race Issue
sections.summary: Lido raised a concern about builder deposits capturing validator funds at the fork boundary; client teams declined to change the spec this late.
sections.body:
- Dima (Lido) described a vulnerability in the one-time builder onboarding process at the Glamsterdam fork boundary: if a 0xB0 builder deposit appears in the pending deposit queue before a validator's 0x01 deposit, the validator deposit becomes a top-up to the builder rather than creating a validator.
  - This introduces a third outcome that existing application-layer protection systems (pre-deposit guarantee contracts) are not designed for: no validator appears at all, and the deposit is effectively lost to the builder.
  - The proposed fix is small: pending deposits with validator withdrawal credential prefixes should always create validators, not credit to builders.
- Multiple client teams and developers opposed making this change now:
  - Barnabas argued it should have been raised 5-6 months ago; the fix was already shipped to Sepolia and Hoodi releases are cut.
  - Lighthouse noted the onboarding cache had bugs and would need to be retested.
  - Lodestar said they would have supported this 1-2 months earlier but had just stress-tested these code paths.
  - Lightclient pointed out the change had already shipped to Sepolia.
  - Changing Hoodi would require delaying several weeks, re-releasing client software, and potentially re-forking Sepolia.
- Pavel (MixBytes) supported the fix from a security perspective, noting that app-layer workarounds are complicated and require extensive auditing.
- Cambridge noted the change is consensus-breaking: if only some clients implement it, it would cause a chain split.
- Decision: no appetite among client teams to change the spec at this stage; the fix was declined for Glamsterdam.
  - Nico Flaig noted that [EIP-8282](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8282) addresses this issue post-fork.
  - Cambridge suggested it might theoretically be possible to make the change between Hoodi and Mainnet, but it would be risky.
  - Dima apologized for the late timing but maintained the fix is important.

sections.heading: EIP-8365: Disabling New 0x00 Validators
sections.summary: Barnabas proposed allowing 0x00 deposits post-fork to create inactive validators instead of burning the ETH; review deferred to a future call.
sections.body:
- Barnabas presented a proposed update to [EIP-8365](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12513), which disables new 0x00 validators after Hegota.
  - Current spec burns ETH from 0x00 deposits made after the fork.
  - Barnabas's proposal: allow 0x00 validators to join but with no validator duties and no earnings; they could perform a BLS change and then be re-queued as a new deposit.
  - This avoids burning ETH from users who deposited before the fork but whose deposits are still in the pending queue at fork time.
- NC raised a counterpoint: invalid signature deposits already burn ETH, so why treat 0x00 deposits differently?
  - NC agreed with the edge case of a deposit made before Hegota that gets processed after the fork, and suggested moving the guard from `apply_pending_deposits` to `process_deposit_request` to grandfather pre-fork deposits.
- The change was very recent; no other teams had reviewed it yet.
- Decision deferred: teams asked to review the proposed changes and revisit on a future call.

sections.heading: EIP-8025: Optional Execution Proofs
sections.summary: Despite strong support from ethrex, Prysm, and provers, CL teams did not reach consensus to CFI EIP-8025; it remains DFI.
sections.body:
- Ignacio (ethrex/Lambda) presented an overview of EIP-8025, which allows opt-in execution proofs to be gossiped and verified on the network.
  - Feature is off by default; no impact on attestation pipeline; validators continue re-executing payloads.
  - On the EL side, 6 clients already pass over 95% of [Hive tests](https://eth-act.github.io/eest-execution-witness-dashboard/#/group/tests-zkevm%20v21.0.1), with changes upstream on main branches.
  - On the CL side, Lighthouse has merged into unstable, Prysm has [an open PR](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17690), and the CL spec already has EIP-8025 as a [feature branch](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/tree/master/specs/_features/eip8025).
  - The EL spec PR is ~16K lines but only 65 lines touch state transition function code; the rest is tests and CI.
- The main argument for CFI: upstreaming the EIP-8025 branch into the EELS main branch would eliminate a year of rebasing overhead and simplify coordination with other features like PBT.
  - The EELS team requires CFI status before merging to main.
- Arguments against CFI:
  - Lightclient argued that CFI/SFI would legitimize the EIP in a way it hasn't earned, and that the branch management argument is not a valid reason to push an EIP through governance; other large features endured the same process for years.
  - Potuz strongly opposed merging into the Heze fork branch, as it would force all future EIP writers to be compatible with optional proof changes.
  - Mario Vega echoed Potuz's concern for the EL specs: merging to main means all other EIPs must adhere to it.
  - Toni Wahrstätter warned that CFI'ing has sunk costs and Hegota is already large.
  - Saulius (Grandine) was open to including it later if scope allows but blocked on FOCIL scope concerns.
- Manu (Prysm) noted that CFI or not would not change Prysm's effort on this EIP, but expressed mild support for CFI.
- Enrico (Teku) initially raised networking concerns (gossip subnet) but was corrected that the gossip participation is also optional (ENR-based opt-in). He ultimately agreed with Potuz's position.
- Lighthouse had merged it into unstable but kingy said it doesn't need CFI to proceed; it's optional and doesn't require a hard fork.
- Several participants noted the existing `_features` directory in CL specs and EELS branches already serve as an experimental area.
  - Spencer (EELS) expressed desire to merge it to the EELS main branch even without CFI, if process allows.
- Decision: EIP-8025 remains DFI for Hegota. Stokes committed to exploring process improvements for long-running experimental features in the EELS repo.

sections.heading: RowDAS
sections.summary: RowDAS was DFI'd due to low blob demand and lack of strong client team support despite a simpler B-variant being available.
sections.body:
- Csaba presented RowDAS, aimed at fixing PeerDAS design decisions: reducing excess CPU load on large nodes and reducing reliance on supernodes.
  - A simpler B-variant exists that only addresses CPU load distribution by standardizing duty allocation in-protocol.
- Main argument against: blob demand is currently low, making this less urgent.
- Rankings: Nimbus was in favor; Teku, Lighthouse, and Grandine were against; Lodestar and Prysm did not submit rankings.
- No client teams spoke up in support during the call.
- Decision: DFI for Hegota, but work should remain ready for when blob demand increases.

sections.heading: EIP-8359: BeaconBlock Reporting Field
sections.summary: EIP-8359 for client diversity reporting via a new BeaconBlock field was DFI'd due to insufficient client team support.
sections.body:
- Luca (Vero) presented on behalf of hanniabu: the EIP proposes a new BeaconBlock field for reporting client diversity data, as the graffiti field is used for other purposes and hurts adoption.
  - Supports complex setups like multi-node and DVT configurations.
  - Opt-out is possible but default is to provide the data.
- The main criticism was that graffiti should suffice; however, graffiti is overloaded and adoption would be lower.
- No client teams spoke in strong favor.
- Decision: DFI for Hegota.

sections.heading: EIP-7716: Anti-Correlation Attestation Penalties
sections.summary: EIP-7716 for correlated downtime penalties was DFI'd; client teams expressed mild interest but not enough to CFI given Hegota's scope.
sections.body:
- Oisin Kyne (Obol) presented EIP-7716, which increases inactivity penalties when many validators go offline simultaneously, scaling up to 256x.
  - Uses a rolling average to bound the duration of increased penalties.
  - Aims to incentivize client and infrastructure diversity; currently 3 clients could individually cause liveness issues if they fail.
  - [Interactive calculator](https://validatordowntime.obol.org/) shared for modeling penalty scenarios.
  - Previously implemented by ChainSafe and Lighthouse; adds one integer to beacon state.
- Obol and ethrex strongly supported CFI.
- Lodestar (Matthew Keil) expressed interest but was concerned about fork size; preferred to leave it as a late addition if time permits.
- Nethermind (Łukasz) was not against it but questioned whether the penalty would change behavior absent a major outage.
- Enrico (Teku) was personally in favor but concerned about interaction with issuance-changing EIPs.
- Barnabé Monnot (EF) was generally opposed due to second-order effects and interaction with consolidation.
- Cambridge raised concerns about how it affects multi-client setups (e.g., 3/5 threshold).
- Ben Adams noted this should be bundled with any emissions changes if those happen.
- Decision: DFI for Hegota. Stokes stated the bar for CFI requires strong support, not mere indifference.

sections.heading: EIP-8205: Withdrawal Credentials Pre-Registration
sections.summary: EIP-8205 for securing delegated staking deposits received mixed support; decision deferred to the next call for further discussion.
sections.body:
- Dima (Lido) presented EIP-8205, which adds a pre-registration mechanism for withdrawal credentials to prevent front-running of delegated staking deposits.
  - The vulnerability affects the majority of Ethereum's staked ETH, which uses delegated staking (Lido, EtherFi, RocketPool, Coinbase, etc.).
  - Current app-layer solutions (pre-deposit bonds, off-chain guardians) are complex, bespoke per protocol, and require ongoing maintenance.
  - Proposed solution: sign a commitment mapping a public key to withdrawal credentials, submit via an EL system contract (similar to EIP-7002/7251), and verify via EIP-4788 at deposit time.
  - CL implementation: four basic operations (add pre-registrations to beacon state, process requests, remove expired ones, add deposit check).
  - EL implementation: a pre-registration request system contract; Lido offered to fund the audit.
  - Spec, tests, and contract code are ready.
- Support voiced by: Teku (Enrico, strong ranking), ACK3 (meditationduck), L2BEAT, MixBytes, Rocket Pool, and multiple security auditors.
- Tomer Ganor (auditor) emphasized that 0x02 migration does not solve the problem: protocols still need to deploy new validators when funds are withdrawn and re-deposited.
- Opposition:
  - Lodestar (Matthew Keil): app-layer solutions exist; concern about precedent of protocol changes for specific stakeholder groups; suggested solving this in the PQ deposit contract redesign.
  - Lighthouse (kingy) and Potuz: agreed it should be fixed alongside PQ deposit changes.
- Barnabas argued the protocol should stay simple and not optimize for delegated staking mechanisms.
- Greg K (Lido) requested the decision be deferred to the next call, arguing the EIP deserved more discussion time.
- Decision deferred to the next ACDC call, where it will be revisited with a 5-minute timebox.
